transformations.rule: Retain the identifying columns and preserve the existing period columns as separate output columns.
transformations.reason: The Data sheet is a wide period table with dates encoded in column names.

transformations.rule: Parse period headers using the cYYYY Mon format and normalize their date interpretation without reordering source period columns unless explicitly requested.
transformations.reason: All period headers follow an explicit year-month naming convention, including nonchronological ordering.

transformations.rule: Preserve explicit numeric zero values as zero and preserve null or missing source cells as null/missing; do not impute values.
transformations.reason: The source contains both explicit zeros and nulls, which have different meanings and must remain distinct.

transformations.rule: Do not exclude or convert negative numeric values if encountered; preserve signed returns in the corresponding period column.
transformations.reason: Signed returns must remain traceable and must not be coerced to positive values.

review: Country has no explicit source column and must remain null.
SKU has no explicit source column; Brand must not be used as a SKU substitute.
The Guide sheet is documentation and should not be transformed as shipment data.
Fact represents the numeric values in the period columns rather than a single source column.
assumptions: Rows in Data beginning at row 2 are detail records.
L1,2 - Division is used as Region because its description identifies it as the region of the country.
L1,1 - Subdivision is used as City/State because its description identifies it as a more specific regional subdivision.
Trade Channel is used as Channel because its column name explicitly describes the channel.
Global Category is used as Category because its description explicitly defines a global category.
Each cYYYY Mon column is a numeric Fact column for the month represented by its header.
guardrails: Result/Total rows excluded from atomic output
